newsitem.title: BELGIUM: BELGIAN ROYALS TO HOLD MEETING ON MISSING CHILDREN.
newsitem.headline: BELGIAN ROYALS TO HOLD MEETING ON MISSING CHILDREN.

text.p: Belgium's King and Queen will hold a "round table" conference on the problems of missing and abused children in the wake of a major paedophile kidnapping and abuse scandal in the country, the palace said on Wednesday.

It said King Albert, Queen Paola and Justice Minister Stefaan De Clerck would meet on October 18 with experts and with families of victims of the scandal in which four girls have so far been found dead and two others rescued.

Several other Belgian girls have gone missing in recent years and it is feared they may have been murdered by members of a gang led by convicted child rapist Marc Dutroux, the key suspect in the scandal which has horrified the whole of Europe.
It was Dutroux who led police to the bodies of the four girls -- two of whom had starved to death.
"This meeting...is aimed at summing up the situation on measures taken and to be taken to fight against this terrible plague," a Palace statement said.
Police have been searching an old mine shaft in southern Belgium since Saturday in their hunt for more bodies or evidence.
